Subject: Acme Health - Private/VPC Post-call recap & next steps

Hi Sandeep - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we stay aligned:

Summary of requirements / pain points:
- Data residency: Acme must keep PHI within US regions only (HIPAA scope).
- Regulatory: security team prefers an air-gapped or private deployment for the pilot; long-term preference TBD.
- Networking: limited outbound egress from app hosts; strict allowlists and no public IPs on internal hosts.
- KMS/HSM: customer-managed key requirement for encryption at rest and key rotation controls.
- Audit & retention: 7 years of audit logs; exportable in native format for audits.

What Redwood can offer (high level):
- Private VPC deployment with VPC peering or transit options, or an on-prem air-gapped package for regulated workloads.
- Support for KMS/HSM integrations and audit log shipping to your SIEM.
- Built-in rollback and model pinning to reduce risk during pilot.

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
1) I will send the private-deployment overview + network checklist (attached).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Marissa (runtime engineer) and your network/security engineers to go through the checklist and connectivity patterns.
3) Procurement: please share initial procurement contacts and any template SOW/PO timeline.

Attachments: redwood-private-deployment-overview.pdf; acme-network-checklist.xlsx

Would love to get the name/email of your network lead so we can loop them into the tech deep-dive. I proposed two time slots in the calendar invite - please accept the one that works.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Camila - thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items and adding context from our side:

1) Air-gap preference: Our compliance team is leaning toward an air-gapped (on-prem) deployment for the pilot because the auditors want complete control over network egress for the initial rollout. Long-term we may open a VPC peering model but that's TBD.
2) Timeline: procurement is aiming for vendor selection by end of Q3. Pilot target: 60 days post-contract.
3) Network lead: please loop in our network engineer Tom Baker (tom.baker@acmehealth.com). He'll own the checklist and any firewall/NAT questions.
4) Security docs: Can you share a short SOC2 summary and typical SOC2 artifacts we can provide to our auditors? Also need an approximate infra footprint (GPU counts / storage) for a small pilot (10 active users, burst loads expected).

I'll have procurement share any contract template we use. Adding them to this thread.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Acme Health - Private/VPC Post-call recap & next steps

Adding technical details from the runtime/ops perspective so Tom and Sandeep have something concrete to review:

- Deployment options:
  * Private VPC: We deploy Redwood control plane in your cloud account with VPC peering or private link. Requires a small set of outbound allowlist IPs for telemetry and updates unless you choose the air-gapped package.
  * Air-gapped (on-prem): offline installer and appliance model. This is fully air-gapped but requires a dedicated on-prem node pool and coordination for patching/upgrade windows. Lead time ~6-8 weeks from PO for a standard PoC.
- Infra footprint (pilot, ballpark): 2x A5000-equivalent GPUs (or 1x A100 for higher concurrency), 1 TB encrypted model storage, and a small control VM (~4 vCPU, 16GB RAM). We can size after a short load-profile call.
- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed KMS and HSMs (PKCS#11). For on-prem HSM integration, we'll need the HSM endpoint details and certs; key rotation processes will be documented in the SOW.
- Networking specifics for checklist:
  * Outbound allowlist: only for control-plane telemetry (if not air-gapped).
  * Ports: 443 for control-plane; SSH (22) only for scheduled maintenance windows if allowed.
  * No public IPs on model-serving hosts in the VPC peer model.

Tom - I'll send the annotated network checklist (acme-network-checklist.xlsx) with inline notes. If an air-gap is required for the pilot, I recommend a separate workshop to cover the offline install/runbook and patch cadence.

I'll also attach a short SOC2 summary and the runbook excerpt for on-prem installation.

- Marissa
